name: Lenalidomide (lower-risk MDS with del(5q))

biomarkers.note: Lenalidomide is used for symptomatic anemia in lower-risk MDS with the del(5q) chromosomal abnormality, with or without additional cytogenetic abnormalities. A TP53 mutation may predict resistance or relapse to lenalidomide. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myelodysplastic Syndromes v3.2026.

treatmentSetting: lower-risk MDS (IPSS-R Very-Low, Low, Intermediate) with symptomatic anemia and del(5q)

eligibilityCriteria.locator: v3.2026, MDS-5 (del(5q) pathway for lower-risk MDS with symptomatic anemia)

drugs.name: Lenalidomide

provenance.locator: Footnote jj on MDS-6A (recommended lenalidomide initial dose is 10 mg/day for 21 out of 28 days, or 28 days, monthly for 2 to 4 months to assess response)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myelodysplastic Syndromes v3.2026, footnote jj (MDS-6A). Lenalidomide 10 mg PO once daily for 21 of 28 days (an alternative is 10 mg/day for all 28 days), given monthly for 2 to 4 months to assess response. Days 1 to 21 models the 21-of-28-day schedule. Use caution in patients with low platelet and neutrophil counts and consider dose modification. Reduce dose in renal impairment (renal excretion).

supportiveCare: Assess response after 2 to 4 months (footnote jj); if no response, treatment is considered a failure and alternatives are considered.
Use caution with low platelet and neutrophil counts; consider modifying lenalidomide dose or schedule.
Lenalidomide requires venous thromboembolism risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis consideration, and pregnancy prevention per the risk-management program.

monitoring: CBC with differential frequently (neutropenia and thrombocytopenia are common early, especially with del(5q))
renal function (dose depends on renal clearance)
response assessment (transfusion independence) at about 2 to 4 months and at 24 weeks

doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt for significant cytopenias and resume at a reduced dose or schedule per prescribing information; cytopenias are frequent in the first weeks in del(5q) MDS. Physician decides.

guideline.locator: Footnote jj on MDS-6A (lenalidomide initial dose 10 mg/day for 21 of 28 days or 28 days, monthly for 2 to 4 months to assess response; caution with low platelet/neutrophil counts); MDS-5 (del(5q) pathway); del(5q) efficacy discussion in manuscript; TP53 as predictor of resistance

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for lenalidomide in lower-risk (IPSS-R) MDS with symptomatic anemia and the del(5q) abnormality. Dose grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myelodysplastic Syndromes v3.2026, footnote jj (MDS-6A): lenalidomide 10 mg/day for 21 of 28 days (or 28 days) monthly for 2 to 4 months to assess response; the 21-of-28-day schedule is modeled (days 1 to 21). del(5q) is the biomarker gate; a TP53 mutation predicts resistance. histology, treatmentIntent and lineOfTherapy are VERIFY.
